title: Geometry - Lesson 6 Practice: Angle Pair Relationships
description: Practice identifying angle pairs and solving missing-angle tasks.

questions.question: Two angles are complementary. One angle measures 38 degrees. What is the other angle?
questions.explanation: Complementary angles add to 90 degrees, so 90 - 38 = 52.

questions.question: Two angles are supplementary. One angle measures 115 degrees. What is the other angle?
questions.explanation: Supplementary angles add to 180 degrees, so 180 - 115 = 65.

questions.question: Vertical angles are always equal in measure.
questions.explanation: Vertical angles are opposite angles formed by intersecting lines, and each pair has equal measures.

questions.question: Two adjacent angles form a straight line. One angle is 47 degrees. Find the other angle. Enter just the number.
questions.explanation: Angles on a straight line are supplementary: 180 - 47 = 133.

questions.question: Which description best identifies adjacent angles?
options: They are opposite each other when two lines cross.
They share a vertex and a side without overlapping.
They always have the same measure.
questions.explanation: Adjacent angles are next to each other and share a vertex and a side.

questions.question: Two vertical angles are formed by intersecting lines. One angle is 126 degrees. Find the opposite angle. Enter just the number.
questions.explanation: Vertical angles are equal, so the opposite angle is also 126 degrees.

questions.question: An angle pair adds to 90 degrees. What is the correct name for the pair?
questions.explanation: Complementary angles have measures that add to 90 degrees.

questions.question: A student says all adjacent angles are supplementary. Explain why this is not always true.
questions.correctAnswer: Adjacent angles share a vertex and a side, but they are supplementary only when they form a straight line. Some adjacent angles can add to 90 degrees or another total.
questions.explanation: The key idea is that adjacent describes position, while supplementary describes a sum of 180 degrees.
